content:
The image shows a soybean stem with:
- Fluffy white/gray mold growth covering a large portion of the stem
- Bleached, whitish coloration of the infected stem tissue
- The lesion appears centered at a node area
- Surrounding leaves are still green
- Pods nearby appear unaffected so far
- The cottony mycelial growth is the dominant feature

This matches White Mold (Sclerotinia stem rot) very closely: fluffy white mold on stems, bleached white stem tissue, lesion at/near a node. The characteristic black sclerotia may be embedded within but aren't clearly visible at this angle, though the white mycelial mass is unmistakable.
